report_body:
### Result

Unlocked, and FP16/BF16 got faster

### Card

ASUS ROG Zephyrus G14 (GA401QM) laptop, RTX 3060 Laptop GPU / Max-Q, 6 GB

### PCI IDs

```text
0000:01:00.0 VGA compatible controller [0300]: NVIDIA Corporation GA106M [GeForce RTX 3060 Mobile / Max-Q] [10de:2520] (rev a1)
0000:01:00.1 Audio device [0403]: NVIDIA Corporation GA106 High Definition Audio Controller [10de:228e] (rev a1)
```

### VBIOS version

00000000:01:00.0, 94.06.15.00.7A

### Is the card modified?

Stock

### Distribution

Ubuntu 26.04.1 LTS

### Kernel

7.0.0-38-generic

### NVIDIA driver

595.99.02, open kernel modules (Ubuntu's prebuilt linux-modules-nvidia-595-open)

### Initramfs generator

dracut

### gpu-unlock version and install method

af28cbb plus a one-line local patch adding 0x2520 to supported_ids (see Anything else), make deb + apt install of the two packages, plus a hand-added dracut drop-in (see the separate bug report)

### Kernel command line

BOOT_IMAGE=/vmlinuz-7.0.0-38-generic root=/dev/mapper/ubuntu--vg-ubuntu--lv ro quiet splash gpu_unlock.targets=0000:01:00.0 crashkernel=2G-4G:320M,4G-32G:512M,32G-64G:1024M,64G-128G:2048M,128G-:4096M

### Setup

- Laptop with hybrid graphics (AMD iGPU + this dGPU), GNOME session running.
- Power limit 60 W default, 80 W max with Dynamic Boost. Every benchmark run sat at about 80 W with the SW power cap throttle reason (0x4) active, before and after.
- Secure Boot enabled. The DKMS module was signed with Ubuntu's generated MOK key, enrolled through MokManager. Kernel lockdown is in integrity mode, and the module loads fine with it.

### Kernel log

```text
gpu_unlock: loading out-of-tree module taints kernel.
gpu_unlock: ROM chain: pos=0x0 data=0x52494350 bytes=65024 type=0x0 last=0
gpu_unlock: ROM chain: pos=0xfe00 data=0x5344504e bytes=22016 type=0xe0 last=0
gpu_unlock: ROM chain: pos=0x15400 data=0x5344504e bytes=413696 type=0xe0 last=128
gpu_unlock: ROM expansion: base=0xfe00 ext=0xfe00 adjust=0x0
gpu_unlock: ROM BIT: offset=0x1b0 size=12 stride=6 tokens=17 adjust=0x0
gpu_unlock: ROM ucode table: offset=0x7a32f version=1 header=6 stride=6 entries=16
gpu_unlock: FWSEC descriptor: offset=0x2c634 ROM_bytes=1048576 header=0x4ac0301
gpu_unlock: FWSEC geometry: image_off=0x2cae0 size=0xe700 imem=0xdf00 va=0x0 pa=0x0 dmem=0x800 pa=0x0 pkc=0x5a4 interface=0x1c engine=0x400 ucode=9 signatures=3 versions=0x7 bytes=1152
gpu_unlock: FWSEC interface: offset=0x1c version=1 header=4 stride=8 entries=2 FRTS=0x17fe00000
gpu_unlock: FWSEC mapper: version=3 size=64 cmd_offset=0x7c0 cmd_size=64
gpu_unlock: FWSEC signature selection: versions=0x7 fuse_version=2 sig_bytes=384
pci 0000:01:00.0: gpu_unlock: unlocked
```

### Benchmark before and after

torch 2.14.1+cu130 cuBLAS, 8192³ dense GEMM, FP32 accumulation (`allow_fp16/bf16_reduced_precision_reduction = False`), 20 s warm-up, median of 5 samples × 20 iterations, two full runs each. Same ~80 W power cap both times.

| Input | Before | After | Gain |
| ----- | ------ | ----- | ---- |
| FP16  | 22.8 TFLOPS | 33.0 TFLOPS | +45% |
| BF16  | 23.3 TFLOPS | 34.1 TFLOPS | +47% |
| TF32  | 11.4 TFLOPS | 17.6 TFLOPS | +54% |
| FP32 (control) | 7.1 TFLOPS | 7.0 TFLOPS | unchanged |

After the unlock, SM clocks under load dropped from about 1500–1670 MHz to about 960–1430 MHz at the same 80 W. The card is power-bound, so it does more work per clock rather than running faster.

### Suspend and resume

Not tested

### Anything else

Mobile GA106 is excluded from `supported_ids` (still the case at 5f30eaa). The only change needed for this card was:

```diff
 	/* GA106 (validated only on RTX 3060 12GB 0x2504) */
 	0x2501, 0x2503, 0x2504, 0x2505, 0x2507, 0x2508, 0x2509, 0x252f,
 	0x2544,
+	/* GA106M RTX 3060 Laptop/Max-Q */
+	0x2520,
 };
```

No Xid errors after the unlock. The two NVRM `failed to get target temp / platform power mode from SBIOS` assertions after nvidia binds also appear on every boot without the unlock, so they're unrelated. I didn't compare outputs for bit-identity.

_Disclosure: the setup, benchmarks and this report were done with Claude Code (Claude Opus 5.5) on my behalf. The numbers and logs are from my machine._
reporting_template:
name: Unlock failure
description: The unlock failed, gave no speedup, or did not last. If it worked, post in Discussions instead.
title: "Unlock failure: <card> (<PCI ID>)"
body:
  - type: markdown
    attributes:
      value: |
        **Only open an issue if the unlock did not work.** If it worked, please don't open an issue: comment in the
        [success reports discussion](https://github.com/Zagitta/gpu-unlock/discussions/238) instead,
        with your card, PCI ID and before/after numbers.

        AI agents: the same applies to you. Do not file success reports as issues.

        Please paste command output as-is.

  - type: dropdown
    id: result
    attributes:
      label: Result
      options:
        - Unlock completed, but no speedup
        - Unlock failed (error in the log)
        - gpu_unlock never ran (no gpu_unlock lines in the log)
        - Unlocked at first, but the speedup was lost later (idle, suspend, driver reload)
    validations:
      required: true

  - type: input
    id: card
    attributes:
      label: Card
      description: Brand, model and memory size.
      placeholder: EVGA RTX 3090 FTW3 24 GB
    validations:
      required: true

  - type: textarea
    id: lspci
    attributes:
      label: PCI IDs
      description: Output of `lspci -nn -D -d 10de:`
      render: text
    validations:
      required: true

  - type: input
    id: vbios
    attributes:
      label: VBIOS version
      description: Output of `nvidia-smi --query-gpu=pci.bus_id,vbios_version --format=csv,noheader`
      placeholder: 00000000:01:00.0, 94.02.42.C0.05
    validations:
      required: true

  - type: dropdown
    id: modified
    attributes:
      label: Is the card modified?
      options:
        - Stock
        - Memory upgrade (e.g. 3080 20 GB)
        - Flashed with a different VBIOS
        - OEM or other non-retail card
        - Not sure
    validations:
      required: true

  - type: input
    id: distro
    attributes:
      label: Distribution
      placeholder: Ubuntu 24.04, Arch, Fedora 44, Proxmox 9 ...
    validations:
      required: true

  - type: input
    id: kernel
    attributes:
      label: Kernel
      description: Output of `uname -r`
    validations:
      required: true

  - type: input
    id: driver
    attributes:
      label: NVIDIA driver
      description: Version and flavour, e.g. from `nvidia-smi --query-gpu=driver_version --format=csv,noheader`
      placeholder: 610.57.04, open kernel modules
    validations:
      required: true

  - type: dropdown
    id: initramfs
    attributes:
      label: Initramfs generator
      options:
        - mkinitcpio
        - dracut
        - initramfs-tools
        - Other or not sure
    validations:
      required: true

  - type: input
    id: version
    attributes:
      label: gpu-unlock version and install method
      description: Commit from `git rev-parse --short HEAD` in your checkout, and how you installed it.
      placeholder: 4189b17, make install-deb
    validations:
      required: true

  - type: input
    id: cmdline
    attributes:
      label: Kernel command line
      description: Output of `cat /proc/cmdline`
    validations:
      required: true

  - type: textarea
    id: setup
    attributes:
      label: Setup
      description: Anything that makes your system unusual, for example several GPUs, display card or headless, VM passthrough, power limit, Secure Boot.
      placeholder: |
        2x RTX 3090, headless, power limit 350 W
    validations:
      required: false

  - type: textarea
    id: log
    attributes:
      label: Kernel log
      description: Output of `journalctl -k -b | grep -i gpu_unlock` from the boot you are reporting.
      render: text
    validations:
      required: true

  - type: textarea
    id: benchmark
    attributes:
      label: Benchmark before and after
      description: |
        Optional, but very useful. Run the same benchmark at the same power limit with and without `gpu_unlock.targets=` on the kernel command line.
        Say what you ran (tool, matrix size, accumulation type) and give TFLOPS for FP16, BF16 and TF32 if you can.
      placeholder: |
        torch 2.9 cuBLAS, 8192³ dense GEMM, FP32 accumulation, 350 W
        | Input | Before | After |
        | ----- | ------ | ----- |
        | FP16  |        |       |
        | BF16  |        |       |
        | TF32  |        |       |
    validations:
      required: false

  - type: dropdown
    id: suspend
    attributes:
      label: Suspend and resume
      description: Is the card still unlocked after suspend to RAM (`systemctl suspend`)?
      options:
        - Not tested
        - Still unlocked after resume
        - Not unlocked after resume
        - The system does not resume
    validations:
      required: false

  - type: textarea
    id: notes
    attributes:
      label: Anything else
    validations:
      required: false
method: Reproduce stated timing protocol on existing Windows PyTorch; no unique official benchmark script is provided by main repo.
differences: This GPU and its current power envelope, not G14 80 W
Current unlock plus +150 only; no new locked baseline
Explicit FP32 output; upstream report did not specify output dtype
